newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Water hampers search for trapped S.Korean miners.
newsitem.headline: Water hampers search for trapped S.Korean miners.

text.p: Rescue workers waded through water in near-freezing temperatures on Thursday searching for 11 miners trapped for nearly 36 hours after a roof collapsed at a coal mine in eastern South Korea, police said.
The death toll from the collapse stood at four, and hope was fast running out to find the 11 trapped miners.
"We found one more dead this morning, but underground water is hampering our rescue efforts," a police spokesman told reporters.

The roof collapsed about noon on Wednesday during blasting operations at the mine in Taebaek, about 200 kilometres (125 miles) east of Seoul, in South Korea's main coal mining area of Kangwon Province.
The roof collapsed at a depth of 335 metres (yards) and about three kilometres from the entrance of the mine.
The blasting operation opened a breach in an underground lake, sending water streaming into the tunnel as well as tons of rubble.
